applicableAreas: Southern property boundary near overhead electric line
findings.comment: Overhead electric line runs along southern boundary with three proposed trees in close proximity (vision analysis). Utility compatibility designation for proposed species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel) is not documented on plans. Clearance distances from tree trunks to outside conductor are not dimensioned, preventing verification that non-utility-compatible trees are beyond 15 lateral feet of distribution conductor.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary near overhead electric line
findings.comment: Proposed Cedar Elm and Live Oak are large tree species typically reaching 40+ feet mature height per ECM Appendix F. Plans show only minimum planting heights (16' minimum container-grown), not mature heights. Large trees are not differentiated from small trees on the landscape plan. Clearance distances from these trees to the overhead electric line are not dimensioned, preventing verification that large trees are beyond 25 lateral feet of distribution conductor.

Overhead electric line is shown on landscape plan but utility pole locations are not explicitly depicted in relation to proposed trees. Clearance distances from tree trunk centers to utility poles cannot be verified.

Pad-mounted transformer locations are shown on Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) but not depicted on Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) in relation to proposed trees. Clearance distances from proposed trees to pad-mounted equipment access doors cannot be verified without overlaying both plans.

Underground electric equipment (pull boxes, vaults, underground transformers) is shown on Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) but not depicted on Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) in relation to proposed trees. Clearance distances from tree trunk centers to underground equipment cannot be verified.

Underground equipment locations and tree locations are shown on separate plans without cross-reference. Cannot verify if any trees are proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground equipment. Root barrier specifications (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) are not documented on landscape plan or details sheets for trees within 20-foot zone.

Proposed Cedar Elm and Live Oak species are large trees that typically reach 40+ feet mature height per ECM Appendix F. Plant schedule shows only minimum container heights at planting (16' HT minimum) but does not state mature heights. Large trees are not differentiated from small trees on the landscape plan, preventing verification of clearances from overhead electric facilities required for large tree species.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary near overhead electric line
findings.comment: Three proposed trees are located in close proximity to the overhead electric line on the southern boundary. Clearance dimensions are not provided on plans, so it cannot be determined whether trees are within prohibited zones (less than 15 feet for non-utility-compatible trees or less than 25 feet for large trees from distribution line). No Austin Energy written approval letter is attached to or referenced on the plans authorizing any trees within restricted clearance zones.
